overview:
Ten tapes, one afternoon in May 1998, and the attic of the aunt who edited them.

Tapes 1–2 stay as they are. They plant everything the later tapes use:
- the player's name, seven apples and the rope in the basket;
- hide-and-seek, with Tonton counting until a slowed Narrator finishes ('Sekiz. Dokuz. On.');
- 1405 carved on the tree;
- a grey man seen for one frame;
- the Rules, the real hand that takes Tonton, and a girl speaking backwards.

TAPE 3 'Tonton Kedi Geri Döndü!' jumps back to over-bright cheer as if nothing happened.
- Tonton is back, stitched, with a GREY tail that Beste insists is orange. He 'repeats' whatever you type, and his sewn mouth never moves.
- In Heykel (statues) you must keep your own mouse still. The grey man exists only in the frozen frames and stands closer each time. The third 'Heykel.' is said in the slowed Narrator's voice.
- Beste teaches the magic word SOBE until an editor's splice cuts her off.
- After the tape, the sheet-covered furniture in the attic has moved a metre closer.

TAPE 4 'Kaybolursan Ne Yaparsın?' is a safety sing-along that drills the home number 364 27 27.
- The last chorus rewrites itself on screen: the number becomes the attic phone's own number, and your 'gelmem' becomes 'gelirim'.
- Beste dials. The real phone behind you rings, and the focus lock keeps you facing the screen.

TAPE 5 'Bugün Sen Beste'sin!' swaps identities.
- The subtitles carry your name and the answer box says BESTE. A talk-show interview collects your answers.
- Asked for 'your' surname, silence wins. Meanwhile the reflection behind her writes SÖYLEME backwards, but only while you look at it.
- A perfect fake ending lowers your guard. Then the real Beste speaks forward from the mirror and teaches you to write backwards so the cartoon cannot read you.

TAPE 6 'İyi ki Doğdun Beste!' claims 14 May as her birthday.
- You opened her birthday present with 0302 minutes earlier, so you can catch the lie. The thing admits it was born that day, in the forest.
- Blowing out the candles kills the real attic bulb.
- The last guest stands behind a chair with your name card.

TAPE 7 'Bir Daha!' is Tape 1 again, as a copy of a copy.
- Each loop changes one thing while the picture rots.
- When the copy is too worn to show anything, Beste is only a voice, and she counts the knocks on your real door.
- In the pristine last pass she turns round without a face.
- Holding rewind un-sticks the loop, which quietly rehearses the finale.

TAPE 8 'Ebe Sensin!' teaches the real rules of hide-and-seek and names the man: EBE.
- Pausing means closing your eyes. While the picture is frozen, something counts to ten as it walks from the attic door to your ear, ending in the exact 'Sekiz. Dokuz. On.' from Tape 1.
- You never find her. One word, 'Sobe', is breathed behind you.

TAPE 9 'HAM KAYIT' drops the cartoon. You search Nermin's edit suite clip by clip:
- the voice session where the cartoon's first line was recorded and the surname was spliced out;
- the Çamlık afternoon where Nermin counted to seven and the trees finished the count;
- a talent form filled in with your own answers, with one empty box (SOYADI);
- Nermin's last recording, made in this very attic and interrupted.
Then the faceless man steps out of the trees wearing Beste's drawn face and says the first line you ever heard.

TAPE 10 'Zamanın Sonu' is the existing finale and asks for the three keys: 1405, 7, Aydın.
- Give all three and you become the ebe.
- Hold rewind instead: the count runs backwards, the real girl is found, and you finally type 'Sobe'.

Dread escalates in four steps:
1. Wrong cheerfulness with cracks (Tapes 3–5).
2. The tape reaching into the room through the phone, the light, the knocks and a count behind you (Tapes 4–8).
3. The tape knowing your answers (Tapes 5 and 9).
4. The documentary truth, with no cartoon (Tape 9).

Rules that hold across all tapes:
- Every gating question gives the truth after three wrong answers.
- The F lock is never released while a tape plays, and the camera never turns on its own mid-tape.
- Each tape owns one mechanic used nowhere else: stillness (3), memory plus a real phone (4), silence, gaze and a fake end (5), contradicting the tape with a document (6), loop difference plus counting real knocks (7), pause as closed eyes (8), clip search (9).
newVoices:
Exactly three new voice styles go into tools/gen_voices.py STYLES, using the same keys as the existing entries.

1) nermin: Aunt Nermin, the show's editor (kurgucu), about 34 in 1998. Warm, tired, slightly hoarse; frightened in her last recording.
- Parameters: base fettah, pitch x1.32, formant x1.09, intonation 0.80, whisper 0.12, speed 0.92.
- As a STYLES entry: dict(model='fettah', speed=0.92, f0=1.32, contour=0.80, formant=1.09, whisper=0.12).
- WHO label 'NERMİN', cls 'anlatici'.
- Her 1998 camcorder lines get a runtime band-limit (about 180–5500 Hz) and light room reverb. Her late attic recording (k9_c4_*) plays at rate 0.95 with no reverb.

2) riza: producer Rıza Yıldız. Gruff, flat and impatient, heard only through a talkback speaker or a megaphone.
- Parameters: base fahrettin, pitch x0.86, formant x0.93, intonation 0.55, whisper 0, speed 1.00.
- As a STYLES entry: dict(model='fahrettin', speed=1.00, f0=0.86, contour=0.55, formant=0.93, whisper=0.0).
- Runtime band-pass 300–3000 Hz ('talkback').
- Label via the per-line 'w' field: KONTROL ODASI (Tape 9 clip 1), RIZA BEY (clip 2).
- He is strictly an impatient boss: no physical presence near the child, no contact.

3) beste_kiz: the LIVING seven-year-old on the 1998 recordings. Natural; less exaggerated than beste and without beste_real's breathiness.
- Parameters: base fettah, pitch x1.58, formant x1.22, intonation 1.00, whisper 0.06, slight vibrato, speed 0.98.
- As a STYLES entry: dict(model='fettah', speed=0.98, f0=1.58, contour=1.00, formant=1.22, whisper=0.06, vibrato=(5.0, 0.01)).
- Label 'BESTE'.

Reused styles (no other new ones):
- The grey man has no style of his own. Every count he finishes is narrator_slow, and Tape 1's n_count_end file ('Sekiz. Dokuz. On.') is reused verbatim in the Tape 8 room count and Tape 9 clip 2. Nermin's line 'O ses sonra bütün kasetlerin anlatıcısı oldu' then explains Tape 1 and every slowed title card after the fact.
- His room lines (k8_count_a, k8_count_b, k8_ebe_sobe) are narrator_slow with label '???' set through 'w'. The Tape 3 'Heykel.' trick is also narrator_slow but keeps the 'ANLATICI' label on purpose.
- Stitched Tonton (Tapes 3–8) reuses tonton / tonton_sad, played at runtime rate 0.93, detune -70.
- beste_real stays the ghost. She is reversed in the hidden messages and speaks forward only on the Tape 5 phone and after-show, the Tape 7 rewind escape, the Tape 8 pause whisper, and the finale.
- beste_kiz is the living girl on tape (Tape 9, and the finale line k10_good_sobe).

Engine notes:
- Add WHO entries for the three new styles.
- Add an optional per-line 'w' label override in lines.json, and d.say(id, {label}).
- Add a per-tape label override for the Tape 5 swap: the label is st.name uppercased and the prompt label is 'BESTE:'.
- New subtitle tokens:
  - {cevap}: the last typed answer, uppercased, plain text, at most 20 characters.
  - {gun}: the player's real weekday in Turkish (Pazar, Pazartesi, Salı, Çarşamba, Perşembe, Cuma, Cumartesi).
  - {yil}: the current year.
- Add a 'room' voice bucket, audio.playRoomVoice(id, {pos, gain, label}), that pauseVoices() and fast-forward do NOT touch.
  - It is used for the Tape 5 and Tape 10 room lines, the Tape 8 paused count, the Tape 8 hot/cold game, and the finale's rewind voices.
  - Voices in it stop on abort and on quit.
- Add these to REVERSED: k3_ters, k4_ters, k6_ters, k7_ters, k8_ters, k9_ters, k10_ters.
  - Each gets a *_rev file. Normal playback plays the _rev file at the moment described; rewinding over the tagged frames plays the forward id. This is exactly the b2_real pattern.
- Line budget: about 300 new lines, many of them short.
  - Every important number is spelled out in 't' and written as digits in 's'.
  - No line is longer than 20 words.

tapes.title: Tonton Kedi Geri Döndü!
tapes.logline: The show restarts as if Tape 2 never happened. The colours are too bright and the jingle plays at full speed. Tonton is back from his 'long journey' with button eyes, a mouth sewn into a smile and a new GREY tail that Beste swears is orange, and he repeats whatever you type. Then Beste teaches Heykel: when the music stops everyone freezes, including you, and every time it stops the grey man is standing a little closer.
tapes.look:
An over-corrected 'restoration', cleaner and brighter than Tape 1, which is exactly the wrong note after Tape 2.
- setBase {saturation 1.25, tintR 1.04, tintG 1.00, tintB 0.94, noise 0.05, tracking 0.15, jitter 0.12, aberration 0.7}; setTapeFx('t1').
- Jingle at Tape 1 speed (152, detune 0); music box tempo 104.
- Freezes: the picture snaps to the 'true' frame (saturation 0.28, jitter 0, tracking 0, noise 0.03, hiss ducked to 30%), a dead-still grey picture. Freeze 3 fades the hiss almost to nothing and adds two soft heartbeats.
- After the game the base settles to saturation 1.10. Goodbye: music box 96, detune -30.
- The splice at the end of the magic-word segment is the first visible 'editor's cut' in the game: six frames of white leader with a grease-pencil X, a dry click and audio dropout, and the VCR counter jumping +37 s.
Compared with Tape 2 there is MORE colour and LESS noise. The decay is now moral, not technical; only the freezes show the grey truth.
tapes.mechanic:
STILLNESS (Heykel). During each freeze the game watches the player's body, not the answer box.
- Counts as moving: an accumulated camera yaw/pitch change above 0.06 rad within any 0.5 s window, any keydown (including Space), or any touch on touch devices. Mouse look is clamped to the TV in focus mode, and the idle breathing sway is position-only, so it is ignored.
- When the player moves, Beste's pupils snap to the viewer while everything else stays frozen.
- The dance lasts a random 6–9 s, so a freeze cannot be anticipated.
- There is no fail state. The result sets st.flags.still (true only if all three freezes were passed) and picks lines.
Twist 1: the grey man exists only in the freeze frames and vanishes the instant the music returns.
Twist 2 (label lie): the third 'Heykel.' is spoken in the slowed Narrator's voice while Beste's mouth moves, and the subtitle label reads ANLATICI instead of BESTE. This is the first hint that the slowed narrator is not who he seems; Nermin explains it in Tape 9.
Twist 3: after the tape the real attic plays Heykel too. The sheet-covered furniture has moved a metre closer to the chair.

Typed question k3_ask_tail.
- turuncu, portakal or oranj: k3_tail_right; st.flags.tail = 'uydu'.
- Anything else: k3_tail_wrong, then k3_tail_again, and ask once more.

segments.beat:
SET-PIECE: HEYKEL. The garden, with a new row of dark pines behind the fence. Rules, then 'Hazır mısın?'.
- Dance: music box at 126; Beste and Tonton bob and sway.
- After a random 6–9 s the music stops dead (stopMusic 0.02) and Beste shouts 'Heykel!'. EVERYTHING freezes: no blinking or breathing, mouths shut, grey frame preset.
- The grey man exists ONLY during freezes and vanishes the instant the music resumes ('Ve dans!').
The three freezes:
- Freeze 1 (5 s): the man is small and far, between the pines behind the fence, alpha 0.55.
- Freeze 2 (6 s): he stands in the middle of the lawn, life-size.
- Freeze 3 (11 s): the call 'Heykel.' is k3_freeze_last, voiced by narrator_slow while Beste's mouth moves; the subtitle label stays ANLATICI. The man stands directly behind Beste and Tonton, his head cropped by the top of the frame, one very long arm hanging beside Beste's shoulder without touching it. The hiss fades almost to nothing; two soft heartbeats. Underneath, very faint, plays the reversed whisper k3_ters_rev (gain 0.35); these 11 s are tagged rev 'k3_ters'.
If the player moves:
- During freeze 1 or 2: k3_moved plays at once (Beste's pupils snap to the viewer, everything else stays frozen) and the freeze continues.
- During freeze 3: k3_moved_last plays and the man's head tilts 15 degrees, the only motion on screen.
The music returns and he is gone.

tapes.secret:
1) 'arkana' (SECRETS label 'Uyarıdaki yazı'): on the warning card at 3.0 s, for 0.2 s, the whole text is replaced by 'ARKANA BAKMA'. Caught by pausing or rewinding. Text: 'ARKANA BAKMA'. It pays off when the sheet-covered chest turns out to have moved behind the player.
2) 'oduydu' (SECRETS label 'Sihirli sözün arkası'): the back of the magic-word card, for 0.25 s during k3_word_cold. Text: 'O DUYDU'.

tapes.clues:
- SOBE (the magic word, spelled on screen and typed by the player) opens the 4-letter lock on the toy chest (Tape 4 find).
- st.flags.still and st.flags.tail ('uydu' / 'direndi') are printed on the Tape 9 talent form ('Kıpırdamadı.' / 'Tonton'un kuyruğu: turuncu').
- The ANLATICI label on a line Beste mouths is explained in Tape 9 clip 4 ('O ses sonra bütün kasetlerin anlatıcısı oldu').
- 'O, kıpırdayanı görür' sets up Tape 8's pause count and its rule 2.
- 'Ve sobelenen kişi...' and 'O DUYDU' set up the man's single 'Sobe' in Tape 8 and the bad ending's 'Şimdi ebe sensin'.
- The reversed k3_ters ('Beni bulursan, sobe de') points to the finale's good ending.
- The splice motif introduces Nermin's interventions (Tapes 5, 8, 9).

tapes.title: Kaybolursan Ne Yaparsın?
tapes.logline: A public-safety episode: stay where you are, never go with strangers, and learn your home phone number with a catchy karaoke song. Beste teaches her own number, 364 27 27. In the last chorus the lyrics rewrite themselves into a different number: the number of the phone in your attic. Then she dials it, and the phone behind you starts to ring while you cannot look away from the screen.

tapes.mechanic:
MEMORY + THE TAPE REACHES INTO THE ROOM.
- A karaoke panel has a bouncing star. The voice stops at a blank and the player types the missing word.
- Then a 7-digit number must be memorised and typed back.
Twist: in the last chorus the panel REWRITES itself letter by letter:
- 'Beste'nin evi' becomes 'senin evin';
- 27 27 becomes 51 80;
- the player's own answer GELMEM becomes GELİRİM.
364 51 80 is printed on the attic phone's dial card from the start, so an attentive player recognises it before Beste says whose it is. Then she dials it, and the real, positional phone behind the player rings during the tape.
The focus lock the player asked for is the scare: you hear it and cannot turn round. F gives only the standard 'Kaset oynarken ekrandan ayrılamazsın.' toast.

SET-PIECE: THE CALL.
1. Beste lifts the cartoon receiver and dials 7 digits (rotaryDial sfx through the TV, a whirr and click per digit, about 4 s; the secret frame flashes during the dialling).
2. 1.5 s of silence.
3. The REAL attic phone (black bakelite, on the cardboard box behind and left of the chair) rings: positional, loud, unfiltered. The bulb flickers once on the first ring (flickerBurst 0.3, respecting 'Yanıp sönmeyi azalt').
4. On TV Beste holds the receiver and stares at the viewer, her eyes tracking the player's gaze; nothing else moves. Ring 2: k4_call1. Ring 4: k4_call2.
5. A prompt opens while the phone keeps ringing behind the player.
6. After the answer, two more rings, then the whisper (high gain, close-mic).
7. She slowly lowers the receiver. The TV hang-up click and the real ringing stop on the same frame, mid-ring.
8. 2.5 s of hiss only, then a snap back to cheerful: music box, smile, the existing b_laugh.
The camera never moves on its own; pressing F gives only the standard lock toast.

tapes.title: Bugün Sen Beste'sin!
tapes.logline: Swap day: you are Beste now, and she is you. The subtitles carry your name, the answer box says BESTE, and she interviews 'Beste' for a pretend talk show, writing every answer in a notebook. The last question is 'Soyadın ne?'. Behind her, a mirror shows a reflection that has stopped copying her, and it is writing something on the fogged glass, but only while you look at it. Then the show ends. Except it doesn't.
tapes.look:
'Cold mirror'.
- Saturation 0.70, tint (0.90, 0.97, 1.10), noise 0.08, tracking 0.30, jitter 0.22, aberration 1.3 (a ghosting double image that suits the mirror).
- Title decay 0.35; jingle 128/-60; music box 90/-90; a short talk-show sting.
- At the surname question: aberration 2.0 and two frames of horizontal flip (canvas scale -1). Each look-away from Beste during that question adds a crack to the mirror glass.
- The fake end card is deliberately bright, and the fake idle screen is a pixel-exact copy of the real one.
- After the fake end, the 'recording under the recording' is grainier and paler: noise 0.14, saturation 0.35, no music, hiss only.
Compared with Tape 4: cold blue instead of yellow, the first ghosting, and the first time the frame itself flips.
tapes.mechanic:
ROLE SWAP where the right move is SILENCE, gated by GAZE, then a FAKE END.
- From k5_rules2 on, Beste's subtitle label is the player's name in capitals and the answer box is labelled 'BESTE:'.
- Every question is an identity question. Every answer is stored (st.answers.age / color / mother / fakeSurname) for the Tape 9 talent form.
- The last question asks for the surname. The correct play is to not answer (the box closes itself after 32 s) or to refuse. Typing 'Aydın' is cut out by Nermin's splice and remembered (st.flags.saidSurnameEarly).
Gaze gate: meanwhile the reflection writes EMELYÖS (SÖYLEME seen backwards) letter by letter, ONLY while the player's gaze dwells on the mirror zone (about 0.6 s of gaze per letter). Beste meanwhile demands 'Bana bak'. Fallback: after 20 s the letters continue on their own (1 per 1.2 s), so touch players and players who never look are not locked out.
Then a FAKE END imitates the end of a tape exactly while the focus lock stays on. The after-show scene adds a one-time REVERSED-TYPING exchange: the real girl can read text typed backwards, the cartoon cannot.

segments.beat:
THE LAST QUESTION. The music stops. A slow push-in: Beste holds the microphone toward the camera (scale 1.4, frozen grin), her face in the left half of the frame and the mirror in the right half. Behind her the reflection breathes on the glass (a fog patch grows) and writes with one finger, in mirror-writing, 'EMELYÖS' (SÖYLEME seen backwards).
GAZE GATE:
- A letter appears only while the player's gaze sits inside the MIRROR rect (about x 420–600, y 80–400) for 0.6 s. The gaze is g.gazeOnTv mapped to TV pixels: px = (gx+1)*320, py = (1-gy)*240.
- Each time the gaze leaves Beste's FACE rect (about x 140–330, y 70–260) for more than 0.6 s, she reacts: k5_look1, then k5_look2, then k5_look3 with a crack in the glass and a red flash. At most three reactions.
- Fallback: after 20 s the remaining letters write themselves (1 per 1.2 s).
The answer box stays open the whole time. Three paths:
- SILENCE (no submit for 32 s): the box closes itself. Beste turns to the mirror and reads the writing aloud as nonsense, which helps the player reverse it, then accepts the silence for now.
- 'AYDIN': a hard SPLICE (white leader, grease-pencil X, VCR counter jump), and the player hears Nermin's voice for the first time, over the cut. Then back to Beste mid-giggle with a 1 s tracking misalignment.
- A fake surname: she 'notes' it, so the player has given away their OWN identity.

tapes.title: İyi ki Doğdun Beste!
tapes.logline: Beste throws herself a birthday party: 'Bugün on dört Mayıs, benim doğum günüm!' The guests are empty chairs, one with your name on it. The eighth candle will not stay lit, and you know her birthday is in February, because you just opened her present with it. Catch the lie and the thing in the cartoon tells you when it was really born. Then it asks you to blow out the candles, and the light in your attic goes out instead.

CATCH THE LIE WITH A DOCUMENT. The decisive question is 'Benim doğum günüm ne zaman?'.
- It accepts the obedient answer ('bugün', '14 Mayıs').
- A player who remembers the school card (Doğum tarihi: 03.02.1991), which they just used to open the gift box, can contradict her ('3 Şubat', '0302').
Catching the lie stops the party and forces the entity to say what it is: 'Şubat, onun doğum günü... Ben on dört Mayıs'ta doğdum. Ormanda.' (st.flags.caughtLie).
Players who play along still learn this later as a whispered 'secret', so nobody misses the reveal. The Tape 9 form records whichever birthday you gave it.

tapes.title: Bir Daha!

It loops, every pass changes one thing, and the picture gets worse. When the copy is too worn to show anything, Beste can only listen, and she asks how many times someone just knocked on YOUR door. On the last, pristine pass she greets you with her back turned, and when she turns round she has no face.

tapes.logline: Night in Çamlık. Beste teaches the real rules of hide-and-seek and a riddle that names the man between the trees: Ebe. Tonight you are the ebe, and to close your eyes you pause the tape. While the picture is frozen, something in your attic counts to ten as it walks from the door to your chair. You never find her. tapes.mechanic:
PAUSE = CLOSING YOUR EYES. The show tells the player to press Space to close their eyes and to keep the tape paused until ten. In Tape 2 pausing was disobedience; now it is the game.
- While paused, director time is frozen, but a real-time room script plays on g.clock timers, through the room voice bucket that pause does not mute.
- A voice counts from the attic door, a floorboard creaks closer, the toy chest lid creaks open, and the count continues right behind the chair. Finally the exact Tape 1 file 'Sekiz. Dokuz. On.' is breathed at the listener's ear.
- Unpausing early is 'peeking': the count restarts once, and the second time sets st.flags.peeked.
- Staying paused much longer is rewarded: the real Beste whispers while the entity cannot see.
- If the player never pauses, the tape pauses itself after 44 s.
The paused frame itself is alive (drawn from g.clock): Beste on the frozen board slowly turns her head to the camera, and a fifth rule fades in.
The camera never turns on its own; 'Arkana bak' is audio only.
